paper_metadata.title: Financial Market Modeling with Quantum Neural Networks

summary: Classical simulation of a Quantum Neural Automaton (QuANN) model of financial market returns. Returns are the product of N binary volatility components V_k in {v0, 2-v0} and a polarization spin sigma in {-1,+1}, each encoded in a qubit whose neural-links operator is a single-qubit rotation parameterised by an angle phi. Simulations use N+1=20 (and 80) components, lambda=1000, 5000-5100 sample trading rounds. Empirical outputs: Fisher-kurtosis tables (Tables 3,5,6,7) and Jarque-Bera normality tests (Tables 4,5) across a grid of (sin^2(phi), v0) in [0.1,0.9] and a noisy-gate variant with Gaussian angle noise (beta in {0.01, 2}). Model reproduces leptokurtic returns, volatility clustering and price jumps for v0<0.87, transitioning to near-Gaussian (v0~0.87) and platykurtic (v0>=0.88) regimes. No quantum hardware or external baseline method; reference distribution is the Gaussian null of the JB test.

experiments.description: Simulation of financial returns from a 20-neuron Quantum Neural Automaton (19 volatility qubits + 1 polarization qubit), lambda=1000, 5100-point runs (first 100 discarded for transients, 5000 analyzed) for a grid of rotation angles sin^2(phi) in {0.4,0.5,0.6} and v0 in {0.4,...,0.9}. Reports Fisher kurtosis (Table 3) and Jarque-Bera normality (Table 4 for sin^2(phi)=0.6; Table 5 for v0=0.87).

algorithm.variant: Recurrent Quantum Artificial Neural Network / Quantum Neural Automaton (QuNA) for financial returns
algorithm.ansatz: Per-neuron single-qubit rotation gates L0=[[sin(phi), i cos(phi)],[i cos(phi), sin(phi)]], L1=[[i cos(phi), sin(phi)],[sin(phi), i cos(phi)]], conditioned on input-neuron firing pattern; full network operator is an ordered product L_N ... L_2 L_1 acting on H_2^{otimes (N+1)}

hyperparameters.initial_state: random U(2) gate per neuron with uniform Haar-like measure

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random U(2) gate per neuron (uniform probability over U(2))

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each volatility / polarization binary degree of freedom is mapped to a qubit; returns operator R = (1/lambda) * prod_k O_k on H_2^{otimes (N+1)} with eigenvalues R(s1,...,s_{N+1}) = (1/lambda) * prod_k v_k(s_k) * sigma(s_{N+1}).

problem_instance.dataset_name: Synthetic QuANN-generated financial-returns time series (no real-market data)

dataset_specification.description: 5100 trading rounds per parameter setting; first 100 discarded; 5000 returns analyzed. Market-making price rule S(t)=S(t-dt) exp(M(t)/lambda) with M(t)=(prod V_k) sigma.

hardware.device_name: Python 3.4 classical simulation of the QuANN state evolution

results.notes: Table 4: sin^2(phi)=0.6, v0=0.87. JB=6.3179, p=0.0425 (only case not rejected at 1%).
Table 5: v0=0.87, sin^2(phi)=0.1. JB=4.8697, p=0.0876 (not rejected at 5%).
Table 5: v0=0.87, sin^2(phi)=0.3. JB=3.8794, p=0.1437 (not rejected at 10%).

speedup_claims.notes: No runtime or complexity speedup claimed. Paper argues QuANN offers a conceptual/expressive advantage (quantum interference reproduces non-Gaussian returns), not a quantitative speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: State-space dim 2^20 for the 20-qubit QuNA; each trading round applies an ordered product of N+1 single-qubit conditional rotation operators.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical simulation cost scales as O(2^N) per round (statevector).

notes: All numeric values read from Tables 3-5 of the arXiv version (v1).
Hardware 'Python 3.4 classical simulation' is stated in Section 2.3 of the paper.
No real-market benchmark dataset; evaluation is statistical (kurtosis, Jarque-Bera) against the Gaussian null.

experiments.description: Extension with stochastic rotation angle phi_k(t)=arcsin(1/sqrt(1+exp(-2 beta z_k(t)))), z_k~N(0,1), producing noisy quantum gates. Simulated for beta in {0.01, 2.0}, v0 in {0.86,...,0.9}, and additionally an 80-component run (79 volatility + 1 polarization) with beta=2, v0=0.9 shown in Figure 3.

algorithm.variant: Noisy-gate QuNA with stochastic Hamiltonian / random rotation angles
algorithm.ansatz: Single-qubit rotations with time-dependent random angle phi_k(t) driven by Gaussian noise z_k(t)~N(0,1) scaled by beta (Eqs. 90-95)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same QuNA structure as exp_1 but with stochastic single-qubit rotation angles per neuron per trading round.

problem_instance.dataset_name: Synthetic noisy-gate QuANN-generated financial-returns time series

dataset_specification.description: Tables 6-7 compare kurtosis and JB p-values for low-noise (beta=0.01) versus high-noise (beta=2) regimes over v0 in [0.86,0.9].

hardware.device_name: Python 3.4 classical simulation with injected Gaussian gate noise

results.notes: Table 6: beta=0.01, v0=0.86. JB p-value=0.0. Paper reports noise level barely affects transition between leptokurtic and platykurtic regimes; number of components dominates the effect.
